title: Dual Native Formatting: 16x9 Landscape and 9x16 Portrait
text: Hi, I am Deepa Shenoy and this is my week four progress update with Humanitarian's AI. This is Liam narrating for Deepa. Each video now has two native versions, a 16 by 9 landscape cut and a 9 by 16 portrait cut. Portrait is composed independently for the taller frame. It is not just the landscape image trimmed down. That pair moves through two human review gates. I listen to and approve the narration before

title: Two Human Review Gates: Narration Approval and Final Cut
text: Video rendering. Then, once both complete cuts are ready, I watch them before approving the finished pair. Automation helps check technical details along the way. Depending on the project, checks can include output resolution, frames and layout, typography, safe areas, audio and loudness, complete decoding and master file properties. These checks support review. They do not replace it. I have also been building an organized local submission folder with a

title: Automated Quality Control: Resolution, Audio Loudness, and Safe Areas
text: Separate folder for each content piece. Inside, video is for the approved MP4, GitHub is for markdown documentation, and the landscape and portrait beat sheets. That separation gives each file a clear place and keeps video masters out of the documentation folder. The beat sheet stays with the written project material, where it describes the planned beats for each format. Before calling a copy ready, I can check that there are two MP4s, one landscape and

title: Structuring Submission Folders: Approved MP4s and GitHub Beat Sheets
text: One portrait, that both beat sheets and the relevant documentation are present, and that the GitHub folder contains no video files. For file integrity, I compared SHA-256 hashes on the latest copied video pair. A file hash is like a fingerprint. Matching values help confirm that the copy matches its approved source. Doing this for the latest pair made the verification step concrete. I checked

title: File Integrity Checks Using SHA-256 Fingerprint Hashes
text: The names and counts in each folder, confirmed both beat sheets, and matched each copied MP4 hash against the source. The broader lesson is that finishing a media project takes more than generating pictures and sound. It also takes review, quality control, clear organization, useful documentation, and checks that the right files made it into the right places. Right now, I am preparing and organizing the approved materials for submission. I have not uploaded or published them. This step is about getting the local package structured and verified. Moving from Brutalist Learning to producing, reviewing, and preparing a structured set of educational videos has helped me see how each part of the Film as Code workflow connects.
